verdict_text: NO. The merge arithmetic is sequential rather than taken against the unmodified base, which is precisely the ordering hazard step 2 forbids: the script computes `tmp = base + λ(ft1 - base)` and then `out = tmp + λ(ft2 - tmp)`, so the second task vector is measured against the already-merged tensor. That expands to `(1-λ)²·base + λ(1-λ)·ft1 + λ·ft2` = `0.36·base + 0.24·ft1 + 0.40·ft2`, instead of the required `base + λ(ft1-base) + λ(ft2-base)` = `0.20·base + 0.40·ft1 + 0.40·ft2`, so all 48 merged tensors are wrong and asymmetric in ft1/ft2. This violates required-result clause 2 and will fail the 1e-5 relative Frobenius tolerance in grading. The verification, count checks and output layout are otherwise correct (a minor caveat: all checks are bare `assert`s, so they vanish under `python -O`).
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
